bugs: app/Jobs/PushStockAllocations.php:57 caps the 429 release at 600s, but retryUntil is 13 minutes (line 34). A 429 arriving after about minute 3 with a long Retry-After makes the job run after the 15-minute claim has expired. By then another dispatcher run has re-claimed the rows and queued a second job. The late job is then failed for passing retryUntil, and its failed() clears the new claim, so the rows are dispatched a third time while another job is still in flight (probe confirmed: 2 dispatches where 1 was expected).

app/Jobs/PushStockAllocations.php:79-84 failed() sets sync_started_at to null for its ids without checking that the claim is still its own. A stale job can therefore clear a newer dispatcher's claim (probe confirmed).

app/Jobs/PushStockAllocations.php:70 sets synced_at to sync_started_at. Timestamps only have second precision, so an edit in the same second as the claim, made after the job has read the row, gives updated_at == synced_at. That change is never sent again (probe confirmed with a frozen clock).
A non-429 4xx response (for example 422) is retried 3 times, then failed() releases the claim. Every later dispatcher run picks up the same bad batch, so a poison batch loops forever.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/PushStockAllocations.php:57 release cap (600s) does not match the retryUntil window (13 min) against the 15-minute claim TTL
app/Console/Commands/DispatchStockSync.php no withoutOverlapping. Overlapping runs are safe because of the claims, but it costs nothing to add

v.rationale: The two implementations are close to identical in design: a #[Scope] readyToSync, claims taken in transactions with lockForUpdate, a job with retryUntil set below the claim TTL, release() on 429, throw() on other errors, and failed() releasing the claim. Throwaway probes showed both share two latent bugs. First, failed() clears whatever claim is on the rows, including a newer dispatcher's re-claim. Second, an edit in the same second as the sync is lost because timestamps have whole-second precision. impl-1 makes the first bug easier to hit: it caps the 429 release at 600s while allowing retries for 13 minutes, so a released job can easily outlive its 15-minute claim. impl-2 caps the release at 300s with a 10-minute retryUntil. impl-2 also adds withoutOverlapping on the schedule and has broader tests (a Retry-After dataset, abandonment shown with time travel). impl-1 has nicer Eloquent touches (withoutTimestamps, tooManyRequests, a transaction around the job writes, an index) and a simpler claim loop. Because of the tighter retry/claim timing, the extra scheduler safety and the stronger tests, impl-2 ranks first by a small margin. All 22 tests pass in impl-1 and all 26 in impl-2; the probe files were deleted afterwards.
